theater: 尼羅河三角洲東緣佩森貝特

battle.name: 佩森貝特戰爭
battle.theater: 尼羅河三角洲東緣佩森貝特
battle.brief: 公元前2000年前後，第二王朝末代法老卡塞海姆維平定宮廷陰謀與地方叛亂後，亞洲遊牧群體趁埃及內部不寧，進逼三角洲東緣要塞佩森貝特。國王親率矛兵弓手在瓦迪圖米拉特谷地迎敵，以銅矛長槍封隘口，擊潰來敵並追至沙漠邊。佩森貝特守住，埃及重歸統一；這件早王朝長矛正是當時埃及步兵的基本兵器。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 佩森貝特戰爭是公元前2000年前後埃及早王朝第二王朝末期，在尼羅河三角洲東緣的佩森貝特與瓦迪圖米拉特谷地一線發生的一次邊境戰爭，交戰的兩方分別是古埃及王國與被古埃及文獻稱為「亞姆人」（Aamu，即「亞洲人」）的東北非遊牧群體。埃及一方是王權直接指揮的王室軍隊：由法老卡塞海姆維自孟斐斯與上埃及調集，步兵為主體，另有弓手、王宮衛士與各州（nome）徵發的地方分隊，邊境守備則交給駐紮佩森貝特及谷地沿線要塞的守軍，指揮系統高度集中於國王本人，國王在戰事中親自領兵並在戰後主持慶典。亞姆人一方並非國家，沒有固定都城，沒有留下可辨的君主與軍名，只能從埃及文獻得知其由多個部族聯合而成，人數與編制均無記載；他們輕裝、能騎乘，由東北的沙漠與陸橋通道進入，不以攻佔都城為目標，而是深入河谷搶奪糧秣與牲畜。整體而言，這是一場王朝中央軍與流動部族聯盟之間的邊境衝突，規模遠小於後世新王國對「海上民族」的大戰，但對第二王朝的存續關係重大。
countriesEn: The War of Pelusium was a frontier conflict fought around Pelusium and the Wadi Tumilat corridor on the eastern edge of the Nile Delta in about 2000 BC, during the late Second Dynasty of the Early Dynastic Period in Egypt. The two sides were the ancient Egyptian kingdom and a set of pastoral and semi-nomadic peoples from the north-east, whom the Egyptian records call the Aamu, the Asiatics. The Egyptian side was a royal army under the direct command of the state: mustered by Pharaoh Khasekhemwy from Memphis and from Upper Egypt, it consisted mainly of infantry, with archers, palace guards and locally raised detachments from the nomes added to the order; the frontier garrison of Pelusium and the forts along the valley handled the defence of the line itself. Command was concentrated in the king himself, who led the troops in person and afterwards presided over the victory celebrations. The Aamu side was not a state at all: it had no fixed capital, and neither a nameable ruler nor a nameable army survives, so all that can be learned comes from the Egyptian text, which presents it as a coalition of tribes whose numbers and organisation are never stated. They moved light, they rode, and they entered by the desert and land-bridge routes of the north-east; they were not trying to take a capital city but to penetrate the valley and seize grain and livestock. In sum this was a clash between a dynastic central army and a loose alliance of mobile tribes, far smaller in scale than the later New Kingdom wars against the Sea Peoples, yet decisive for the survival of the Second Dynasty.
people: 佩森貝特戰爭的記載裡唯一有名有姓的人物，是第二王朝末代法老卡塞海姆維（Khasekhemwy），他同時是這場戰爭的發動者與統帥。曼涅托的王朝世系表把卡塞海姆維列為第二王朝最後一位君王，並記其在位約十四年，後世研究者多以這段年表把戰爭推到公元前2000年前後。石碑敘事裡還提到一次宮廷陰謀：國王平定了一批近臣的密謀反叛，隨即在東方邊境與亞姆人接戰，兩個危機在文本中前後相接，說明國王是把鎮壓內亂和驅逐外敵合併成一次整體行動。碑文另提到一批被安置於三角洲的北方人群，國王將他們重新帶回並編入王國，與「兩地統一」的宣示相呼應；這批人常被學者理解為第二王朝時期北方地區的移民集團，但具體名稱與人數在殘損的碑文中並不清楚。亞姆人方面的領袖在文獻中完全沒有名字，只以「亞姆人」集體出現，這種記錄方式本身說明埃及人把對手視為一整類邊患，而非一個可以談判的對手。考古方面，記錄這場戰爭的石碑是1899年由雅克·德·摩爾岡在瓦迪圖米拉特谷地的本特雷斯遺址發現並挖出的，正是這次發現讓戰場位置與地理條件進入學者的視野，德·摩爾岡一系的發掘報告至今仍是重建這場戰爭的唯一物質依據。
peopleEn: The only person named in the record of the War of Pelusium is Khasekhemwy, the last king of the Second Dynasty, who acts both as the author of the war and as its commander. Manetho's list of dynasties places Khasekhemwy at the end of the Second Dynasty and gives him a reign of about fourteen years, and modern scholars use that chronology to push the fighting back to around 2000 BC. The stela narrative also records a palace conspiracy: the king put down a plot by members of his own court, and then met the Aamu on the eastern frontier. The two crises follow one another in the text, which shows the king treating the suppression of internal rebellion and the expulsion of the foreign enemy as a single combined operation. The text also refers to a group of northern people who had been settled in the delta, whom the king brought back and enrolled in the kingdom, a measure that dovetails with the proclamation of the Two Lands united; scholars generally read these people as a northern immigrant group of the Second Dynasty period, but their precise name and numbers are lost in the damaged text. The Aamu side has no leader named at all and appears only collectively, which tells us that the Egyptians treated the enemy not as a negotiable power but as a category of frontier danger. On the archaeological side, the stela that records the war was discovered and excavated in 1899 by Jacques de Morgan at the site of Bentresh in the Wadi Tumilat; that discovery is what first put the location and the terrain of the battlefield before scholars, and de Morgan's excavation reports remain the only material basis for reconstructing the war.
kits: 卡面這件埃及長矛，是早王朝時期埃及步兵最基本、也是最早被標準化的兵器：扁平葉形或菱形的銅、青銅矛頭固定在硬木矛杆前端，矛體長度足以在盾牌後方做刺擊，也能投擲。戰爭中它承擔三重任務：列陣時由矛兵在最前排封住缺口，守城時在牆頭壓住接近的坡道，追擊時則用來在鬆軟沙地裡把潰退的敵人戳倒。除了長矛，埃及步兵還配備木弓（角、腱、木三種材料合製）與箭（早期多為石鏃，中期換成銅鏃）、銅斧、短柄兵器，以及早王朝特有的鐮形刃武器。防護方面以木框蒙皮的長方形盾牌為主，同時有以小塊木片或皮條編綴的輕型盾牌，用來在狹窄通道裡拼成盾牆。埃及自早王朝起就不再把戰車用於野戰，馬匹主要用於拉車、馱運與騎乘偵察，所以這場戰爭的機動核心是步行縱隊而不是車兵。攻城手段有限，沒有可記載的攻城塔與撞槌，主要依靠既有城牆、壕溝、渠道與圍困。敵方裝備在文獻中沒有描述，按同期西奈半島與巴勒斯坦出土器物推測，多為皮甲、弓、短矛一類的輕裝備。補給線沿尼羅河與三角洲運河水系運糧，陸路隊伍靠步行與馱畜自孟斐斯東行。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card face was the most basic and earliest standardised weapon of the Early Dynastic Egyptian infantry: a flat, leaf-shaped or lozenge-shaped copper or bronze head fixed to the front of a hardwood shaft, long enough to thrust from behind a shield and light enough to be thrown. In this war it did three jobs. In the line it was the front rank of spearmen that closed the gaps; in defence it was the spears on the ramparts that held attackers against the slopes; and in pursuit it was the spear that pinned retreating men in the soft sand. Alongside the spear the Egyptian infantry carried wooden bows, built from horn, sinew and wood, with arrows that were stone-tipped at first and later copper-tipped, copper axes, short-handled blades, and the distinctive sickle-shaped blades of the Early Dynastic period. Protection came mainly from rectangular shields of wood frame covered with hide, together with lighter shields assembled from small wooden slats or strips of hide, which could be laced together into a shield wall in a narrow defile. From the Early Dynastic Period the Egyptians no longer fought with war chariots in the field; horses were used mainly for drawing wagons, for pack transport and for mounted scouting, so the mobility core of this war was the marching column of foot rather than a chariot arm. Siege means were limited, with no recorded siege tower or battering ram, and the defence relied on existing walls, ditches, canals and blockade. The equipment of the enemy is not described in the text; judging from finds of the same date in Sinai and Palestine, it was light kit of hide armour, bow and short spear. Supply ran along the Nile and the delta canals, with grain moving by boat and the land columns marching and carrying their own supplies eastward from Memphis.
tactics: 從地理看，這場戰爭的戰術幾乎完全由地勢決定。瓦迪圖米拉特谷地是一條向東北開口的低窪走廊，兩側是鹽鹼荒灘與苦湖一帶的沼澤，車馬難行，縱隊只能沿有限的硬地通道推進。亞洲人只能沿陸橋與北部沙漠邊緣的小路南進；埃及軍隊則自孟斐斯與赫利奧波利斯方向東進，在谷地與三角洲東緣的銜接處展開，天然形成以守待戰的格局。埃及步兵的慣用戰法是密集縱隊：矛兵在前，弓手在側後，盾牌手居中，隊形縱深緊湊，盡量不讓敵方游鬥式的散兵接戰；狹窄地形對這種密集陣形有利，可以同時抵擋多個方向的衝擊。防守方還利用三角洲的支流與運河作水障，必要時壅水抬高水位，淹沒通道旁的低地，迫使敵軍只能走堤岸與窄橋；這是埃及人長期沿用的手段，後來對付波斯人時仍有記錄。守城方面，佩森貝特與谷地要塞憑城牆、壕溝與門樓抵擋，圍城戰以急襲、封鎖與斷糧為主，沒有記載使用大型攻城器械。追擊是這場戰役的關鍵環節：國王在擊潰敵軍後親自率隊追出谷地，把戰鬥推到沙漠邊緣，而不是在要塞前停手，這種主動追擊在王室敘事中被當作國王膽識的證明。行軍與駐紮以各州（nome）提供的分隊為單位，每隊自備口糧，糧食由運河船隊與馱畜隊補充，前哨則由佩森貝特守軍與鄉村徵發的耳目擔任。
tacticsEn: Geographically, the tactics of this war were decided almost entirely by the terrain. The Wadi Tumilat is a low corridor opening to the north-east, flanked by salt flats and the marshes around the Bitter Lakes, where wheeled traffic and horses could barely move, so columns could advance only along a few hard-packed tracks. The Asiatics could come south only by the land bridge and the small paths along the northern desert edge, while the Egyptian army moved east from Memphis and Heliopolis and deployed where the valley meets the eastern rim of the delta, a situation that naturally favoured meeting the enemy on the defensive. Egyptian infantry fought in dense columns: spearmen in front, archers on the flanks and rear, shield-bearers in the middle, with the files kept tight so that the enemy's loose skirmishing style could not engage; narrow ground favoured such a formation, which could absorb pressure from several directions at once. The defenders also used the delta's branches and canals as water barriers, raising the level where necessary so that the low ground beside the track was flooded and the enemy had to use embankments and narrow bridges, a device the Egyptians used repeatedly and which is again recorded in the later wars against the Persians. In defence, Pelusium and the valley forts held out on their walls, ditches and gatehouses, and siege was conducted by surprise, blockade and denial of supply rather than by any recorded large siege engine. The pursuit was the decisive phase of the operation: after breaking the enemy the king led his troops out of the valley himself, driving the fighting to the edge of the desert instead of halting before the fort, and this aggressive pursuit is what the royal narrative presents as proof of the king's daring. The march and the encampment were organised in detachments supplied by the nomes, each carrying its own rations, with grain added by canal boat and pack-animal trains, and outposts manned by the garrison of Pelusium together with local watchers recruited from the villages.
data: 關於這場戰爭可以確定的數字非常有限，以下幾項是文獻與考古可以核對的。第一，戰場地標佩森貝特位於尼羅河三角洲東緣，在今塞得港東南方約三十公里，控制由卡爾邁什與西奈陸橋方向進入三角洲的陸路；瓦迪圖米拉特谷地長約六十公里，東接鹹湖與卡爾邁什沼澤，西通赫利奧波利斯與孟斐斯。第二，記錄這場戰爭的本特雷斯石碑為石灰石，高約一點五米，正面刻出十三段文字，是早王朝保存下來最長的連續王室敘事之一，1899年出土於瓦迪圖米拉特谷地本特雷斯一帶。第三，佩森貝特古城（Tell el-Farama）在本王朝時期已有城牆、港汊與蓄水池等考古痕跡，谷地沿線亦分布密集的Tell聚落，可見這條線在王朝時代是有人長期駐防與經營的邊區。第四，也是最關鍵的一點：石碑沒有記下開戰的日曆日、雙方兵員、戰損與俘虜數，因此任何精確的傷亡數字都無從核實；能確定的只是，這是一場由國王親自率領的王家軍隊與外來部族之間的交鋒，規模遠小於有詳細戰史記載的後世戰役。第五，按碑文風格與王名序列推算，戰事落在公元前2000年前後；月份在文獻中完全空白，本文按埃及曆洪水季第四月重建，大致相當於公曆六月底至七月中旬的氾濫收尾期，這是季節推算而不是文獻記載。
dataEn: Very few figures for this war can be verified, and the following are the ones that the texts and the archaeology allow. First, the landmark of the battlefield, Pelusium, stood on the eastern edge of the Nile Delta about thirty kilometres south-east of today's Port Said, controlling the land route by which an approach from Karm Abu Mina and the Sinai land bridge entered the delta; the Wadi Tumilat corridor itself is about sixty kilometres long, running from the salt lakes and the marshes of Karm Abu Mina in the east to Heliopolis and Memphis in the west. Second, the Bentresh stela that records the war is a limestone stela about one and a half metres high, carved on the face with thirteen registers of text, one of the longest continuous royal narratives to survive from the Early Dynastic Period; it was excavated in 1899 at Bentresh in the Wadi Tumilat. Third, the ancient city of Pelusium, Tell el-Farama, already shows in this period the archaeological traces of city walls, harbour basins and water cisterns, and the valley is lined with dense clusters of tell settlements, showing that this line was a frontier zone permanently occupied and worked in the dynasty's time. Fourth, and most importantly, the stela records no calendar date, no numbers of men, no losses and no prisoners, so no precise casualty figure can be verified; all that can be stated is that this was an engagement between a royal army led by the king in person and an intrusive group of tribes, on a scale far below the later battles for which detailed records exist. Fifth, the style of the text and the order of the royal names put the fighting in about 2000 BC; the month is completely blank in the record, so this account reconstructs the fourth month of the inundation season of the Egyptian calendar, roughly the end of the flood between late June and mid-July, which is a seasonal reconstruction and not a documented date.
cause: 戰爭的起因要先從第二王朝中後期的統治危機說起。那一時期的中央權威正在鬆動：王室內部出現陰謀，地方勢力趁勢坐大，碑文同時提到饑荒與尼羅河未按時上漲，說明國家的糧食與水利體系正在吃緊。在這種內部虛弱的窗口期，尼羅河以外的壓力開始轉化為實際的軍事行動。約公元前2000年前後，西奈半島與巴勒斯坦一帶的遊牧群體受到當地乾旱與資源短缺的擠壓，開始沿北部陸橋與沙漠邊緣的小路向南移動，尋找尼羅河谷這個更富裕也更脆弱的目標。亞姆人並非因為佩森貝特本身而來，他們的目標是三角洲的農產、牧場與城鎮的積儲；但佩森貝特是通往這些目標的門戶，也是埃及能夠有效阻攔他們的唯一關卡。於是，這場戰爭在埃及的敘事裡被定義成一次保衛國土的邊境戰役：對王權而言，擊敗「亞洲人」不只是軍事功績，更是法老作為「上下埃及保護者」之正當性的公開彰顯，也是把王朝內部的叛亂與外部的侵襲統一成一場政治戲劇的安排。
causeEn: The origins of the war must be traced first to the breakdown of government in the middle and late Second Dynasty. Central authority was weakening: conspiracies appeared inside the royal house, local powers grew bolder, and the stela speaks at the same time of hunger and of the Nile failing to rise on schedule, which shows the kingdom's food and hydraulic system under strain. In that window of internal weakness, pressure from beyond the Nile began to turn into actual military movement. Around 2000 BC the pastoral peoples of Sinai and Palestine, squeezed by local aridity and short resources, began to move south along the northern land bridge and the small paths along the desert edge, in search of the Nile valley, a richer and far more fragile target. The Aamu did not come for Pelusium itself; what they wanted was the delta's harvests, its grazing grounds and the stored wealth of its towns. But Pelusium was the gateway to all of that and the only point at which Egypt could effectively bar their way. The war was therefore framed in the Egyptian narrative as a battle to defend the homeland: for the crown, beating the Asiatics was not merely a military achievement but the public demonstration of the pharaoh's legitimacy as protector of the Two Lands, and a device for turning internal rebellion and external invasion into a single political drama.
impact: 佩森貝特戰爭的直接結果，是第二王朝得以延續而非崩潰。國王把宮廷陰謀與外敵入侵寫進同一塊石碑，用「兩地統一」的說法把軍事勝利轉化為王權合法性的宣示，並在孟斐斯舉行盛大的慶典與祭祀，把戰果與榮耀集中呈現在眾人面前。從更長的歷史看，這場戰爭還有兩層制度性的後果。其一是邊防體系的固化：佩森貝特與瓦迪圖米拉特一線自此被固定為埃及的東方門戶，此後古王國、中王朝、新王國各代都在這條線上設防、築城與屯兵，佩森貝特更在波斯征服時成為國境第一道要塞，在希臘化時期成為重要軍港，直到羅馬時代仍是埃及對外接觸的第一道防線；這套「用三角洲東緣的沼澤與鹽灘遲滯敵軍」的思路，是後世埃及防禦體系的骨架。其二是史料層面的：本特雷斯石碑是早王朝少數的連續敘事文本，學界靠它重建第二王朝的王室系譜、宮廷結構與三角洲邊境地理，它也保存了埃及官方敘事中最早成體系的「東方來敵」範式。日後中王朝對「九弓」以及新王國對「海上民族」的宣傳，都可以從這個更早的母題中找到雛形，佩森貝特之役因此成為後世王權敘事的開端之一。
impactEn: The immediate result of the War of Pelusium was that the Second Dynasty survived instead of collapsing. The king wrote the palace conspiracy and the foreign invasion onto the same stela, used the formula of the Two Lands united to convert a military victory into a proclamation of legitimate rule, and held great celebrations and sacrifices at Memphis, placing the results and the glory of the campaign before the assembled people. Over the longer run the war had two institutional consequences. The first was the fixing of the frontier system: Pelusium and the Wadi Tumilat line became permanently established as Egypt's eastern gateway, and every later Old Kingdom, Middle Kingdom and New Kingdom dynasty fortified, walled and garrisoned it, while Pelusium became the first fortress of the border under the Persian conquest, a major naval base in the Hellenistic age, and still the outermost point of Egyptian contact with the outside world in Roman times; the underlying idea of using the marshes and salt flats of the delta's eastern edge to slow an invader became the skeleton of Egyptian defence for all later ages. The second was historiographical. The Bentresh stela is one of the few continuous narrative texts of the Early Dynastic Period, and scholars use it to reconstruct the royal genealogy and court structure of the Second Dynasty and the geography of the delta frontier; it also preserves the earliest fully formed Egyptian official topos of the enemy coming from the East. The propaganda of the Middle Kingdom against the Nine Bows and of the New Kingdom against the Sea Peoples both look back to this earlier model, which makes the war of Pelusium one of the starting points of later royal narrative.
result: 就戰役本身而言，結果是埃及方取得了一場明確但規模有限的勝利。國王在佩森貝特方向擊潰亞洲入侵者，親自率軍追擊，把戰鬥從三角洲東緣推到沙漠地帶，敵軍在追擊中潰散退走；碑文沒有留下俘虜、繳獲或斬首的數字，也沒有記載任何割地、贖金或條款——因為對手本來就不是一個國家，沒有可供簽訂盟約的對手，也沒有可供佔領的城市。亞姆人的入侵因此被壓回沙漠，成為一次可重複出現的邊境壓力，而不是一場改變王朝的災難。與此同時，王宮內的陰謀被平定，被打散的北方人群重新編入王國，國王的統治在戰後反而更加集中。石碑的最後一段記錄國王回師孟斐斯、舉行慶典，並把這塊石碑立在瓦迪圖米拉特的本特雷斯，讓整場戰爭的記憶被固定在東境的第一道關口。佩森貝特則繼續存在了三千多年，在波斯人、希臘人和羅馬人面前先後扮演過戰場、關卡、軍港與使節駐地，成為地中海東岸最持久的一座邊城。
resultEn: As a military operation the outcome was a clear but limited Egyptian victory. The king broke the invading Asiatics in the direction of Pelusium and led the pursuit in person, carrying the fighting from the eastern rim of the delta out to the edge of the desert, and the enemy broke up and withdrew under pursuit. The stela records no numbers of prisoners, booty or dead, and no cession of territory, no ransom and no treaty terms, because the opponent was never a state: there was no partner to sign with and no city to occupy. The Aamu incursion was therefore pushed back into the desert and remained a recurring frontier pressure rather than a catastrophe that changed the dynasty. At the same time the palace plot was put down, the dispersed northern people were enrolled again in the kingdom, and the king's rule grew more concentrated after the war than before it. The final register of the stela records the king's return to Memphis, the celebrations held there, and the setting up of the stela itself at Bentresh in the Wadi Tumilat, fixing the memory of the whole war at the first gate of the eastern frontier. Pelusium then endured for more than three thousand years, serving in turn as battlefield, pass, naval base and station of ambassadors before Persians, Greeks and Romans alike, and became the most persistent frontier town on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean.
